title: People’s Mañanera October 14
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Decree to Protect Children and Adolescents Online  
** Platforms will have 30 days to implement measures against violent, sexual,
and harassing content, verify ages, and strengthen privacy protections. The
measure aims to ensure safe digital environments, without censorship or
restrictions on political content.

**Sembrando Vida: A Program Unique in the World  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum explained that the program will continue
throughout her six-year term in office. Over 1.2 billion trees have been
planted, with a goal of planting 1.5 billion by 2030.

**Housing for Well-being: An Asset for Mexican Families  
** The Infonavit housing agency has delivered 45,100 homes in 27 states. In
Quintana Roo, progress is being made toward reaching 80% of the goal of 62,000
homes, benefiting mothers, young people, and working families.

**Sheinbaum Addresses IMSS Workers’ Demands  
** A plan was put in place to guarantee the supply of pharmaceuticals, address
the regularization of the employment status of personnel hired during the
pandemic, and improve residency scholarships. The President also called for
free and pressure-free union consultations.

**Jalisco: Calls for an Investigation into Allegations of Repression and
Torture  
** The President asked the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) to
thoroughly investigate the arrests that occurred during protests for clean
water in Jalisco and to clarify the use of tear gas and water cannons. “There
can be no torture in Mexico,” she explained.

**Fact Check: Misinformation on Health, Security, and Pemex**

  * It is not true that Mexico’s healthcare system has collapsed and is in crisis.
  * It is not true that “soldiers disguised as ‘doctors’” were sent to “break up” the demonstration by Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) healthcare workers.
  * It is not true that there is a shortage of medications in the Ministry of National Defense (SEDENA).
  * It is not true that there is waste leakage in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Regional General Hospital No. 1 in Ciudad Obregón.
  * It is not true that Aeroméxico withdrew from Tulum due to security and profitability issues.
  * It is not true that there is a fuel shortage at gas stations in Mexico City.
  * It is not true that President Sheinbaum is inviting investment in Pemex.
